problem:
Find the Laplace transform $L{{f}^{″}(t)}$ for $s>3,$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ ${f}^{′}(0)=4,$ $f(0)=2,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{2s-4}{{s}^{2}-4s+3},\,s>3.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}$ piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}L{f(t)}-sf(0)-{f}^{′}(0).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{″}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{″}(t)} & ={s}^{2}\cdot \frac{2s-4}{{s}^{2}-4s+3}-s\cdot 2-4 \\  & =\frac{2{s}^{2}(s-2)}{{s}^{2}-4s+3}-2(s+2) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{{s}^{2}(s-2)-({s}^{2}-4s+3)(s+2)}{{s}^{2}-4s+3} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{({s}^{3}-2{s}^{2})-({s}^{3}-2{s}^{2}-5s+6)}{{s}^{2}-4s+3} \\  & =\frac{10s-12}{{s}^{2}-4s+3}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>3.$
